references.text: Joseph was accused by Potiphar's wife, who cried for help when no one was nearby, an example of a false accusation in contrast to the innocent woman in Deuteronomy 22:27
Jephthah describes how the children of Israel cried for help, but no one saved them, using similar language about crying out and having no savior
David cries for help, but there is no one to save him, a similar situation where cries for help go unanswered
Isaiah describes the vineyard and the expectation of justice, but hears a cry - the same theme of crying out with no one coming to rescue
The Lord sees that there is no one to intervene and no savior, the same theme of lacking someone to save
The preceding verse describing another situation where the woman did not cry out, in contrast to this verse where she cried out in an open field
